title: Coral and the Kitchen
premise: Yara Hartwell, a marine biologist who retreated to the coastal town of Saltmere after a devastating betrayal, inherits half of a failing orchard from a grandmother he barely knew—only to discover the other half belongs to Coral Reyes, the childhood friend his family wronged and the woman he never stopped loving. As they are forced to co-manage the stubborn land to satisfy the deed's conditions, Yara confronts the corrupt family legacy that exiled Coral's family and learns that his lifelong strategy of emotional containment is its own form of cowardice. When a developer offers a fortune to raze the orchard, Yara must publicly renounce his inheritance and his name's power, choosing to stay past the point of no return. In the end, Coral stays too, and they rebuild the orchard—and each other—together.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez is a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets in kitchens from Oaxaca to Portland. She now lives near the sea, where she grows citrus badly and believes every romance should taste like salt and sugar in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Yara, counting sea turtles to avoid counting his losses, receives notice that his grandmother left him half an orchard—co-owned with Coral Reyes, the name he's spent ten years avoiding. His POV; the beat is dread disguised as indifference, the first crack in his trained containment.

chapters.title: Salt on the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Yara arrives at the orchard and finds Coral already there, furious and unafraid, holding the same deed. Coral's POV reveals a childhood of exile his family caused. The emotional beat is old wounds reopened under new light—neither will sell, neither will leave.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Forced to co-sign every decision, they negotiate an uneasy truce: split the harvest, split the land, never speak of the past. Yara's POV; the beat is brittle humor masking attraction, as working the trees together makes avoidance physically impossible.

chapters.title: What the Roots Remember
chapters.summary: Coral uncovers letters proving Yara's grandfather cheated her family out of their half a generation ago—and that his grandmother spent years trying to atone. Coral's POV; the beat is grief transmuted into resolve, and the first time she sees Yara as something other than his surname.

chapters.title: A Muscle Like Any Other
chapters.summary: A storm floods the low orchard; they work all night sandbagging the roots, and Yara admits, almost, why he left Saltmere. His POV; the beat is the heart's containment theory failing in real time as he realizes he's been training himself to feel nothing.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: A development firm, backed by Yara's own estranged father, offers a fortune for the orchard—and a clean legal path to evict Coral. Yara's POV; the beat is temptation sharpened into horror as he recognizes his family's corruption reaching for him through the deed.

chapters.title: Harvest of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Coral discovers Yara's father forged her signature years ago to consolidate the claim, and that Yara knew the family history and said nothing. Her POV; the beat is betrayal layered on betrayal—she chooses the orchard over him and stops speaking to him.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Yara confronts his father, publicly refuses the buyout, and hands his lawyer the evidence of the forgery—sacrificing his inheritance and his family's power to restore Coral's full claim. His POV; the beat is the climax: staying visible, staying accountable, expecting nothing back.

chapters.title: What Stays After
chapters.summary: The deed is corrected; Coral owns the orchard outright and Yara owns nothing but his apology. Coral's POV; the beat is the slow thaw—she watches him plant new trees on rented ground beside hers, and lets him explain what his silence was protecting and what it cost.

chapters.title: First Fruit
chapters.summary: A year later, the orchard bears its first real harvest under shared stewardship; Coral asks Yara to stay for good, not as an heir but as a choice. Alternating POV in the final scene; the beat is belonging earned rather than inherited—two names on one deed, finally true.
